scene.speaker: freya
scene.bubble: Let's count everything! One sun, two shoes, three birds… and one Pip!
scene.intro: Freya wants to count everything in the lighthouse! One sun in the window, two shoes by the door, three birds on the roof, four spoons on the table. Pip helps her — but Pip counts the same fish five times, so the numbers are always wrong! How many books can you see? How many hands have you got? Count with Freya from one to ten, and then count everything in YOUR room!

activities.title: Match the number with the word.

words.clue: A dog has this many legs.
An octopus has this many arms.

activities.title: Listen and count with Freya. Write a number in each gap.

data.script: Freya: Let's count! How many pencils? One, two, three. Three pencils! … Nico: How many birds in the tree? … Freya: One, two, three, four, five! Five birds. … Nico: And how many legs has Pip got? … Freya: Two! Birds have two legs. … Nico: How many biscuits on the plate? … Freya: Ten! No, wait… nine. Pip is eating one!

activities.title: Quick check · Choose the correct number.

data.text: Count things in the classroom with your partner: windows, doors, bags, shoes. "How many windows? Two!"

activities.title: A and B are not the same. Find out why!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 12 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Count at home and write: how many doors, beds, chairs and spoons. There are…

outcomes.puede: Follow classroom instructions; identify familiar words in songs and short spoken sentences.
Greet; say name, age, colours; name objects; answer yes/no questions.
Recognise all 26 letters; match words to pictures (family, food, animals, body).
Write own name; trace and copy words; label pictures (3–5 words).
~150 productive words; Verb to be, can, like + noun, imperatives, this/that.

gramatica: Subject pronouns: I, you, he, she, it
